explorationReceipt.approximateInspectedScope: Approximately 58 named tracks, release cuts, reviews and catalogue references across Juno's live September 2026 electro and experimental/electronic windows, Freaking Tricks, Kyiv label Lisosmuha, Studio Barnhus, EC Underground and Keplar's remastered Arovane catalogue. Written metadata and attributed descriptions only; no audio audition.
exclusions: Recent Runs 193–201 source fields, canonical identities, active placement-specific rejects, untriggered PARKED revisits, prior unresolved titles, prior ranked leads, exact alternates and global utility identities were excluded.

The five-run repetition check avoided every boundary planned in Runs 197, 198 and 201 and the recurring Cave → Abundance, Raataja → Crawl and Rabbit Hole → Can I live cluster. Each placement pair was re-derived from the current 52-track ledger and checked for adjacency.

Top slots represent a straight repeated-vocal proposition, a harsh broken-beat proposition and an overlooked nonlinear/proto-dubstep catalogue proposition. This is information-gain ranking, not a role or style quota.

Current electro/experimental pages also exposed generic release-level IDM, ambient and straight techno material; entries lacking a credible track-specific belonging proposition or not likely to change a passage were inspected but not promoted.
The protected Transparency → When We Froze → Stardancer sequence remains untouched. No Spotify connector, raw audio, audio-feature inference or invented identity was used.
sourceWindows: CURRENT RELEASE WINDOW: Juno's live electro page supplied the September 10 False Shuffle EP and September 11 LIS 003 compilation with exact tracklists and differentiated track descriptions. https://www.juno.co.uk/electro/this-week/

ADJACENT / EMERGING WINDOW: Kyiv label Lisosmuha's LIS 003 artists and Studio Barnhus debut-album material supplied harsh broken-beat, glitched and shuffling propositions outside the recent techno-only scan. https://www.juno.co.uk/electro/this-week/ ; https://www.juno.co.uk/experimental-electronic/this-week/

OVERLOOKED / NEWLY CONTEXTUALIZED WINDOW: Keplar's September 9 remaster of Arovane's 1999 Atol Scrap supplied exact nonlinear, ambient-dub and proto-dubstep catalogue paths newly in circulation. https://www.juno.co.uk/experimental-electronic/this-week/
